fixes.explanation: Right, it's False. The text says, “But the magicians did the same thing by their magic arts, and they also brought frogs up onto the land of Egypt.” (Exodus 8:7) They did the same thing as Aaron, Moses' brother. Land already covered in frogs, and their big move is more frogs. Keep that in mind, because the story doesn't stop here.

Tomorrow! Pharaoh, Egypt's king, answers Moses, “Tomorrow.” (Exodus 8:10) Frogs in his palace, his bedroom and his bed, and he picks tomorrow. Friend, I'd have said "tonight, please, I'll hold the door myself."

Sunset is a decent guess, but the text gives one word. When Moses, Israel's leader, asks Pharaoh, Egypt's king, when to pray, Pharaoh answers, “Tomorrow.” (Exodus 8:10) No hour is given. Just tomorrow, baker.

No hopping home. The text says the LORD did as Moses, Israel's leader, requested, and “…the frogs in the houses, the courtyards, and the fields died.” (Exodus 8:13) The next verse says they were piled into heaps. It's a heavy moment, baker, so let's treat it that way.

Softening would have changed the whole story, but it's not what happens. When Pharaoh, Egypt's king, sees there's relief, “…he hardened his heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron…” (Exodus 8:15) Moses is Israel's leader, and Aaron is his brother. Pharaoh dug in instead.

It's True. The text says that Pharaoh, Egypt's king, “…hardened his heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.” (Exodus 8:15) Moses is Israel's leader, and Aaron is his brother. The frogs are gone, Pharaoh won't listen, and it all goes just as the LORD said.

The dust! The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to say to Aaron, “Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth…” (Exodus 8:16) Not water this time. Just plain ground-level dust. Then verse 17 says all the dust of the earth turned into gnats. Friend, I've swept up plenty of dust, and I never once checked it for gnats.

No rock in this passage. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to say to Aaron, “Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth…” (Exodus 8:16) Aaron is Moses' brother. The staff hits the dust, and then the text says gnats came upon man and beast (Exodus 8:17).

Not even a few. The text says, “The magicians tried to produce gnats using their magic arts, but they could not.” (Exodus 8:18) Zero gnats from them, while the gnats Aaron's staff brought stayed on man and beast. They came up empty, baker.

That's what they say. “This is the finger of God…” the magicians tell Pharaoh, Egypt's king. (Exodus 8:19) These are the same magicians who did the same thing with the frogs, so that line is quite something. They called it the finger of God.

False is right. The text says, “But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.” (Exodus 8:19) His own magicians say, “This is the finger of God,” and Pharaoh, Egypt's king, still won't listen. Friend, even that doesn't move him.
